text.p: Enterprise Oil Plc said its alliance in the Gulf of Mexico with Pennzoil Co, announced on Thursday, would benefit both companies.
"It's a classic win-win," Enterprise international exploration director Andrew Armour told Reuters.

Armour said the deal, under which Enterprise will contribute funds towards drilling costs in exchange for half of Pennzoil's interest in 102 of the U.S. company's leases in the Gulf, had been under negotiation since February.

He said the move meant a rebalancing of Enterprise Oil's exploration portfolio, increasing its presence in the Gulf, where good prospects and extensive infrastructure offer potentially quicker returns than more frontier-type areas.
"They (Pennzoil) recognise that we have a lot to bring, including money," Armour said.

He said Enterprise would bring exploration skills. "The geological setting is one we are very familiar with," he said, citing similarities with what Enterprise does in the North Sea in such fields as Arbroath and Nelson.

Enterprise had studied ways of increasing its presence in the Gulf of Mexico for a year, he said, adding the alliance fitted with Pennzoil, which is seen to be expanding internationally and focussing on development rather than exploration in the Gulf.

Four wells are already being drilled and Armour said although he hoped to see successful results by the end of the year, he expected to wait a little longer. He said successful drills in the area are of the order of one in five or six made.

Because of the extensive production infrastructure in the area, Armour said successful wells see "rather speedy cash flow". He said 18 months was viewed as a long time for development in the area, with finds sometimes coming on stream in as short a time as two or three months.

Enterprise, which will be opening an office in Houston, will contribute a minimum of $100 million through to 1997 to the project, which will take up 25 percent of the company's annual exploration budget.
Armour noted that the Pennzoil properties, unlike leases which expire after a certain time, are held on a production basis.
